lawyer:
Md. Abdur Rashid, Advocate ----- for the Petitioner 
Kazi Ebadul Haque, Advocate ----- for the Opposite party
parties:
Anwara Begum
Vs.
Maimuna Khatun Chowdhury & Other
full_judgment: 9. It was found by the learned District Judge that the pre-emptor-O.P. No. I was a non-notified co-sharer. Her case was that she purchased the share of her sister Unune Salma by kabala dated 21-7-73 Ext. 1(Ga) and that when she went to her father's house in village Mohammadpur on 14.8.73 to possess her purchased land she came to know of the transfers made by her brothers to the petitioner. She was corroborated by her son P.W. 2. The learned District Judge upon a consideration of the oral evidence and the circumstances of the case, particularly the strained relationship between the pre-emptor and her brothers came to the conclusion that there was no reason to disbelieve her (pre-emptor's) case regarding the date of knowledge. The learned Advocate for the petitioner has argued that the evidence of the O.P. No. 1 was vague in that she did not state from whom she had learnt about the transfers. The allegation seem to be unfounded because the O.P. No. 1 clearly stated in cross-examination that she had learnt about the transfers from her son and other persons. The learned Advocate has then argued that the courts below ought to have drawn a presumption adverse to the pre-emptor for not examining one Moklesur Rahman and Saleh Ahmed from whom P.W. 2 was alleged to have learnt about the transfers. The learned Advocate has sought to reinforce his submission by referring to a decision reported in 1981 BLD 56. In that case the evidence as to the date of knowledge was given by the pre-emptor alone and the courts below accepted his evidence. But in this court it was observed that since the pre-emptor's son, who was allegedly present when the knowledge of the transfer occurred, was not examined and no explanation was given for his non-examination, the courts below failed to exercise their jurisdiction in not drawing an adverse presumption on that account and further that the pre-emptor had 'failed to prove the date of his knowledge and as such the application was barred by limitation. With respect, I would like to observe that I do not find any aspect of jurisdiction being involved in the alleged failure of the courts below to draw an ad-'verse presumption as held in the case cited and contended by the learned Advocate. Moreover, the facts of the case referred to are entirely different from that of the present case. In the instant case the evidence of the pre-emptor was corroborated by that of her son P.W 2. The District Judge also referred to the circumstances of the case while assessing the evidence of the O.P. No. 1 on the point. Moreover, there could not be any question of examining Moklesur Rahman and others by the O.P. No. 1 because these were the persons who were said to have resisted the preemptor's son from possessing the land in question pursuant to her purchase from Umme Salma. Having regard to the evidence on record and the findings of the courts below arrived at upon a proper consideration there-of I am not at all impressed by the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner which is accordingly rejected.
